help.papers-that-expire.step6: Driver app, riding without a fleet: the same button sends the card to network staff, who read the same photo and record the date, or tell you why they could not. You are told either way.
help.papers-that-expire.note1: Nothing is written into a record as “grounded”: the date is the switch in both directions, so a renewal takes effect the moment it is recorded and there is nothing to unwind.
help.papers-that-expire.note2: A card a driver sent is opened by the office of the fleet they drive for and by network staff — not by another fleet, and not by a colleague. A card that is not accepted is deleted at once; one that is recorded is kept as the licence’s own copy, and replaces the one before it.
help.papers-that-expire.note4: A sender can ask for a carrier with insurance cover. Your carrier insurance counts once SeeBuyGet has read it off the policy you sent, with what it covers and up to how much a load: from then until it lapses, loads that ask for cover are open to your drivers, and their consignment notes name the cover. Without it, those loads say why they are closed.
help.papers-that-expire.note5: Riding for yourself, you can show your own insurance cover: send your policy from the Driver app, under Your insurance cover. Once SeeBuyGet has read it, loads whose sender asks for cover are open to you until it runs out, and your consignment notes name it. A fleet’s driver is covered by the fleet’s policy.
help.papers-that-expire.note3: A driver who is in no fleet — taken off one, or left — has nobody to send a card to, and cannot start a shift until a fleet offers them a place.
help.hand-back.title: Hand a load back before pickup
help.hand-back.summary: The office can put a load on a driver, so a driver must be able to say no — and a driver who claimed a load can change their mind. Until the goods are on the vehicle a load can be handed back: it goes back on the market as if untouched, the sender’s charge comes back, and the reason is on the record.
help.hand-back.step1: Driver app, My loads: open the load as if to collect it and tap “I cannot take this load”. Say why — a breakdown, a road, a change of plan — and hand it back. It leaves your list.
help.hand-back.step2: Shop app, Freight you posted: the load shows who handed it back, when and why, and is on the market again. Any charge for it has come back. Nothing has moved.
help.hand-back.step3: Fleet app: the office that put the load on the driver is told too, with the reason, and can put it on somebody else from Dispatch.
help.hand-back.step4: Once the goods are on the vehicle this is no longer the way out: a load that has been taken over is delivered, or the sender is asked to withdraw it.
help.hand-back.note1: Every hand-back stays on the load’s record with the driver’s reason — it is not a rating, and it is not hidden either.
help.hours-of-service.title: The shift limit and rest between shifts
help.hours-of-service.summary: A shift has a limit — 13 hours — after which no new load is offered, shown as takeable or put on a driver, though what is already aboard is delivered. After a real working day of four hours or more, the next shift waits for 9 hours of rest.
help.hours-of-service.step1: Driver app, Home: the clock on the shift shows the hours on duty against the limit. Past it, the board marks every load, no offer comes, and the start screen says so plainly.
help.hours-of-service.step2: The driver is told without asking: a notice less than an hour before the limit, and another at the limit, saying what is still theirs to do (deliver what is aboard), what is not (anything new), and that the next shift can start 9 hours after this one ends. The clock on the shift says “less than an hour left” in that last hour.
help.hours-of-service.step3: Driver app, starting a shift too soon after a working day: the start is refused, and the refusal says how many hours since the last shift ended and how many are needed. A coupling of a few minutes — a wrong scan, a short move — owes no rest.
help.hours-of-service.step4: Driver app, Home, after a working day: the start screen says from when the next shift can start, before anything is tried. Press “Tell me when I can start” to get a notice at that moment. Somebody who tries to start too early is told at that moment as well. Nobody else is: for most working days it falls in the night.
help.hours-of-service.step5: Fleet app, Dashboard and Shifts: a driver over the limit is marked. Dispatch will not put a load on them; end the shift and let them rest.
help.hours-of-service.step6: Fleet app, the bell: the office is told when one of its drivers passes the limit, with the vehicle, so that no new load is planned for them.
help.hours-of-service.note1: The limits are the network’s, between the EU’s daily driving limit and its reduced daily rest, and they are not a claim about any country’s law. Where a jurisdiction sets its own, that becomes the limit.
help.goods-coming-back.title: Have your goods brought to your door
help.goods-coming-back.summary: A parcel of yours withdrawn at a hub comes back to the shop you handed it in at, and the shop asks for the way back as it hands it over. While it is still at the hub, a driver can bring it to your door instead, paid first by M-Pesa.
help.goods-coming-back.step1: Send app, My parcels: the parcel bringing your goods back says “Your goods, coming back”. While it is still at the hub, tap “Bring it to my door instead”.
help.goods-coming-back.step2: Say where your door is — a street, a gate, a landmark — and “Find it”, or put the pin on the map yourself. Then the most you allow a driver: a figure is suggested, and a driver may ask less, never more. And your M-Pesa number: the driver calls it at your door.
help.goods-coming-back.step3: “Ask M-Pesa for …” and approve it on your phone. Once it is paid, a load to your door waits for a driver. Not paid in time, or “Give up: it comes to the shop”, and it comes to the shop as before; while it is still at the hub, you can ask again.
help.goods-coming-back.step4: While no driver has taken it: “Raise the most” — approved on your phone the same way — or “Send it to … instead — all of it back”, and you pay for it in cash at the shop as you collect it. Once it is delivered, what the driver charged less than you paid goes back to your number with the next payout.
help.goods-coming-back.note1: Where it cannot come to your door, the app says so, and why, before you pay anything. It then comes to the shop as before.
help.call-off-order.title: Call an order off
help.call-off-order.summary: A store can call an order off from its own app while its parcel is not on the road: not handed in yet, at the shop it was handed in at, or at a hub. What comes back, and what it costs, is said before anything is done.
help.call-off-order.step1: Store app, Orders: open the order and tap “Call this order off”. It says what calling it off would do now and what it costs; nothing is done yet. “Keep it going” leaves it as it was.
help.call-off-order.step2: Not handed in yet, or still at the shop it was handed in at: “Call it off”. It is withdrawn, and what you paid for it comes back to your balance.
help.call-off-order.step3: At a hub: it comes back to the shop it was handed in at, as a new parcel at the price shown — “Bring it back for …”. What it cost to get it to the hub is not given back. Collect it at that shop with the code on the new order.
help.call-off-order.step4: At a hub, and never handed in at a shop — collected at your door, or brought to the hub in bulk: say where it comes back to. A shop, found by its name or area, nearest first; or “Your door”, as a load: give the most you pay a driver, and the first driver whose vehicle fits takes it at their price, never more. The load is under Sent as freight.
help.call-off-order.note1: On the road, waiting at the shop for the buyer, or collected, an order cannot be called off: the app says why. A parcel bringing your goods back to you cannot be called off either — collect it at the shop it goes to.
help.hub-hours.title: Say when your hub is open and how to reach it
help.hub-hours.summary: Drivers bringing or collecting bags, and stores bringing parcels, see in their apps when your hub is open, who to ask for, where to come in, and a button that calls you.
help.hub-hours.step1: Hub app, home screen: “Opening hours and how to reach you”. The hub’s owner taps “Set your hours and contact” — later, “Change hours or contact”.
help.hub-hours.step2: Tick “Open on set days and hours” and give each day’s hours. Give a number to call — your desk or your gate, not the number you sign in with — and, if you like, a second number, who to ask for and where to come in. Then “Save”.
help.hub-hours.step3: Your public page shows your hours either way. Your number and where to come in are on it only if you tick “Show my number and where to come in on my public page, for anyone”; drivers and stores working with your hub see them in their app either way.
help.hub-hours.note1: Your number is never printed: it is shown as a button that calls you. Without hours, nobody is told when you are open; without a number, nobody can call you from the app.
help.logistics-directory.title: Be found in the logistics directory
help.logistics-directory.summary: SeeBuyGet’s public directory lists forwarders, clearing agents, container depots and hauliers whose papers our staff checked, by country. Say whether you are shown, write your own line, and choose how people reach you.
help.logistics-directory.step1: Business app: “Business details” › “In the logistics directory”. Fleet app: the “Fleet” screen, the card “In the logistics directory”. It says whether you are shown, and if not, why.
help.logistics-directory.step2: Tap “Change” and write your line: what you do and where, in your own words, up to 240 letters. “Save”. It is shown as your own words, beside what we have seen of your work on SeeBuyGet.
help.logistics-directory.step3: How people reach you: a business shows its contact entry, on the same screen; a fleet fills in the phone, email and website it wants shown under “Change” — leave a box empty to show nothing there. A phone is shown as a Call button.
help.logistics-directory.step4: “Take us off the directory” takes you off at once; “Show us in the directory” puts you back, with your line kept. “See the directory” opens your country’s page.
help.logistics-directory.note1: The list is alphabetical and nobody pays to be on it or higher on it. What we have seen counts only work done through SeeBuyGet, and the page says that a short record is not a bad one.
help.logistics-directory.note2: A business is shown once two of our staff have checked its papers, and only if it forwards, clears goods or runs a container depot. Changing its name or registration number takes it off until it is checked again. A fleet is shown once it is active. In a business, only an owner changes this.
help.logistics-directory.note3: Your country is on the directory’s map where its firms’ own places are. In the Business app, add one under “Business details” › “Your places” › “New place”: a pin on the map, or an address we can find.
help.logistics-directory.note4: Choosing a clearing agent for an import or an export, the list is the directory’s: every clearing agent our staff checked, its own words beside what we have seen, the papers checked — never one that took itself off the directory.
help.logistics-directory.note5: Looking for a carrier: Business app, “Your carriers” › “Find a haulier”. Call or write to one, or tap “Ask for a contract”: the haulier is told in its Fleet app, once a week at most. When it agrees, it taps “Record a contract with …” on that notice, and the contract comes to you under “Offered to you”: an owner taps “Accept”, with no code, or “Decline”. Nothing is agreed by asking, and the haulier is told your answer.
help.logistics-directory.note6: Anybody can search the directory across every country, without an account: on the directory’s page, under “Find a firm, in any country” — a few words, every one of which must be found on the firm, and what it does. The address keeps the search, so it can be shared.
help.hub-carriers.title: Send pallets, cages and crates to other hubs
help.hub-carriers.summary: Say what your hub moves bags on to other hubs, and send them with a driver — saying how they come back: with the driver, left there, or on a return job you post.
help.hub-carriers.step1: Hub app, home screen: “Pallets, cages and crates”. The hub’s owner taps “Add a kind”: what it is, its name as your people call it, its length, width and loaded height in centimetres, and what it may carry in kilograms. How many parcels it holds is worked out from those.
help.hub-carriers.step2: Under “Carriers between hubs”, “Send carriers with a driver”: which, how many, to which hub, and how they come back — with the driver on the same visit, left there for the other hub to keep or use, or kept there for a return job you post and pay. Scan the pass of the driver who takes them, then “Send them”. The other hub is told what to do with them.
help.hub-carriers.step3: Carriers another hub sent you are under “Come to you”. Do what it asked: “Counted back out to the driver”, with how many went back — never more than came; “Taken in: they stay here”; or “Kept aside for their return job”.
help.hub-carriers.step4: Yours kept at another hub are under “Yours, away”. The owner taps “Post the return job”, with what they weigh together: a load from that hub back to you, on the board for any driver and priced as any load. You pay the carrier, between the two of you.
help.hub-carriers.note1: Only the hub’s owner says what the hub moves bags on and posts a return job. The people on the floor send carriers with a driver and count them back out.
help.hub-space.title: Say how much your hub can take, and what happens when it is full
help.hub-space.summary: Two numbers tell the network how much your hub can take: how many bags can stand on your floor at once, and how many parcels you sort in a day. When your floor is full, new bags go to another hub for your areas, or wait where they are and come by themselves when you have room.
help.hub-space.step1: Hub app, home screen: the card “Your floor” says how many bag places are free of how many, how many parcels you sort a day, and how many you have sorted today. The hub’s owner taps “Set your space” — later, “Change”.
help.hub-space.step2: “Bag places”: count every bag that can stand on your floor at once — bags that came in and wait to be sorted, and bags you are filling or that wait for a driver. A folded empty bag takes no place.
help.hub-space.step3: “Parcels sorted in a day”: what your people sort on a normal day. Then “Save”. A hub signing up says both on its first steps, and changes them here any day.
help.hub-space.step4: When the floor is full the card says “Full”. New bags for your areas go to another approved hub that serves them; where there is none, they wait at the shop or hub that holds them, and come to you by themselves, the oldest first, as you sort and send bags on.
help.hub-space.note1: A driver who brings bags is never turned away: every bag is taken. Past your places the card says “Over full” in red — sort, and send bags on, to make room.
help.hub-space.note2: When today’s sorting is full, the card says “Day full” and you are told in your bell. New bags go to another hub with room today where there is one; the others still come to you, and what is not sorted today is sorted tomorrow.
help.hub-space.note3: Why bags on their way count too: a bag offered to a driver, or on the road to you, takes a place the moment it arrives. Counting only what stands on the floor would send every waiting bag the minute one place came free.
help.hub-space.note4: Only the owner, signed in as the hub, sets the two numbers. The people who work the floor see them; SeeBuyGet staff see them and change nothing. Until the owner says them, nothing is held back for the hub.
help.bag-waits.title: A bag that waits for room at its hub
help.bag-waits.summary: A closed bag is offered to drivers only where the hub it goes to has room on its floor. When that hub, and every other hub for the same area, is full, the bag waits where it is and goes on by itself when there is room.
help.bag-waits.step1: You close the bag as always. Where its hub has no room, the bag screen says it waits here for room at that hub, and your bell says so too — once.
help.bag-waits.step2: Keep the bag on your floor. It is offered to no driver, and no driver can take it across the counter, while it waits.
help.bag-waits.step3: When the hub has room — it sorts and sends bags on, or its owner gives it more places — the bag is offered to drivers again by itself, the oldest waiting bag first, and your bell tells you it can go on.
help.bag-waits.note1: Where another approved hub serves the same area and has room, your bag goes there instead, and does not wait at all. The driver’s offer names the hub it goes to.
help.bag-waits.note2: Why it waits with you rather than going anyway: a driver would arrive at a hub with no room on its floor. A bag already on its way is still taken at the hub.
help.install-app.title: Install the app and get its notifications
help.install-app.summary: Installed, a SeeBuyGet app opens from your home screen like any other app, full screen, and can tell you the moment something needs you. Until it is installed, a bar pinned at the top of the app says “Install the … app”: tap it for the steps, each with a drawing.
help.install-app.step1: Tap the “Install the … app” bar, or “How” on it. A sheet opens with numbered steps for the phone in your hand. Wrong phone? Choose Android or iPhone under “Your phone”.
help.install-app.step2: Put it on your home screen. Android: tap “Install now”, then Install — or, where that is not offered, Chrome’s ⋮ menu at the top right, then Install app or Add to Home screen. iPhone, in Safari: Share at the bottom of the screen, then Add to Home Screen, then Add.
help.install-app.step3: Open the app from its new icon on your home screen — on an iPhone, never from Safari. Tap “Turn on notifications”, on the app’s home screen or under the bell at the top, and when the phone asks, tap Allow.
help.install-app.step4: Said no, or nothing arrives? Android: hold the app’s icon for two seconds, tap ⓘ for App info, then Notifications, and turn them all on. iPhone: open Settings, then Notifications, then the app, and turn on Allow Notifications.
help.install-app.step5: Notifications come late? Many Android phones hold apps back to save battery. In the app’s App info, tap Battery, then Unrestricted — some phones say No restrictions, or Allow background activity.
help.install-app.step6: On Android the bar goes by itself once the app is installed. On an iPhone, Safari cannot tell: once the app is on your home screen, tap “It is on my home screen” in the sheet.
help.install-app.note1: Notifications turned off later, or held back by the battery? The same guide stays in the app: in the Shop, Hub, Driver, Fleet and Store app, tap your picture, then “Get the most out of the app”; in the Send app, “Account”, then “Get the most out of the app”; in the Business app — whose bar is on its Overview, and shows at a computer too where Chrome or Edge can install it — tap your initials at the top right, then “Get the most out of the app”.
help.install-app.note2: An iPhone shows the app’s notifications only when the app was opened from its icon on the home screen, and only on iOS 16.4 or later.
help.install-app.note3: On an Android phone, hold the icon of the installed app for its shortcuts, each straight to one screen. Shop app: take in a parcel, hand over a parcel, hand to the bus, receive a bag. Hub app: coming in, drop a bag, sort parcels, load a bag onward. Driver app: find work, my loads, the freight market, earnings. Fleet app: dispatch a load, shifts, runs, orders. Store app: ship an order, orders, dock, bookkeeping. Send app: send a parcel, track a parcel, my parcels. Business app: loads, exports, imports, parcels — a section your business does not do opens its Overview.
help.install-app.note4: Where the phone shows one, a number on the app’s icon counts the notifications not yet read.
help.install-app.note5: Why install: on the home screen the app opens in one tap, full screen, and its notifications reach you even while it is closed, so you need not keep it open to be told.
help.install-app.note6: Every one of these apps keeps its notices under the bell at the top, read or not. Allowing notifications only makes the phone tell you as each one comes.
help.get-around.title: Move around the app: Back, sheets and refreshing
help.get-around.summary: The apps move the way your phone’s own apps do. Back closes what is open, then goes back a screen; a sheet closes with a swipe down; and pulling down at the top of a screen fetches it again.
help.get-around.step1: Back — an Android phone’s Back button or Back gesture — closes an open sheet or menu first, then goes back one screen. On the app’s first screen, with nothing open, Back leaves the app.
help.get-around.step2: A sheet that slides up from the bottom closes with a swipe down, or with Back.
help.get-around.step3: Each screen keeps your place: go back to a list, and you are where you left it.
help.get-around.step4: Shop, Hub, Driver, Fleet, Store and Send app: pull down at the very top of a screen and let go, and it is fetched again.
help.get-around.step5: Business app: a load’s record is in parts — “Overview”, “On the road”, “Papers”, “Payment” and “Claim”. The names stay pinned at the top as you scroll; tap one, or swipe the record left or right.
help.get-around.note1: In a load’s record, a dot beside a part’s name marks something there that waits for you. Whatever waits for your answer is in “Overview”.
help.get-around.note2: The screen stays on while you scan, while a code is held up to be scanned, and while a driver’s run is on the road.
help.get-around.note3: A swipe that starts at the very edge of the screen is the phone’s own Back gesture, not a swipe between parts.
help.get-around.note4: Shop, Hub, Driver, Fleet, Store and Send app: before you sign in, a bar at the bottom of the screen holds Back, Help, Read aloud and All apps. Once you are signed in, the app’s own tabs take its place.
help.share-seebuyget.title: Share SeeBuyGet with the people you work with
help.share-seebuyget.summary: Every app has a link to SeeBuyGet that is your own, to send to whoever you like. It opens as a card with a picture and a line about SeeBuyGet, and whoever signs up through it is counted to you.
help.share-seebuyget.step1: Shop, Hub, Driver, Fleet and Store app: tap your picture, then “Share SeeBuyGet”. Business app: the menu under your name, then “Share SeeBuyGet”.
help.share-seebuyget.step2: Tap “Share”: your phone’s own share list opens, with your contacts and the apps on the phone. Choose who to send it to.
help.share-seebuyget.step3: Or tap an app under “Or send it with” — WhatsApp, Telegram, a text message, email — listed in the order people share where you live. “Copy the link” copies it, to paste in any chat.
help.share-seebuyget.step4: Where the phone lets the app read your contacts, “Pick from your contacts” adds people, each with a button that messages them straight.
help.share-seebuyget.note1: Your link is made once and stays the same, however often you send it. The sheet says how many people joined through it.
help.share-seebuyget.note2: Somebody who opens your link and signs up on that phone within thirty days — on the front page, in the Send app or in the Business app — is counted to you.
help.share-seebuyget.note3: Send app: “Account”, then “Invite a friend”. Pick friends from your contacts or add one by name, choose how to send, then tap “Send” beside each name.
help.share-seebuyget.note4: The contacts you pick never leave your phone: the app only opens your messaging app with the link in it.
help.fingerprint-unlock.title: Unlock the app with your fingerprint or face
help.fingerprint-unlock.summary: On a phone of your own, the app can open with your fingerprint or face, the way you unlock the phone — instead of your PIN, or, in the Shop, Hub and Store app, the account’s password. It is turned on and off under Settings, and the PIN or the password always works too.
help.fingerprint-unlock.step1: Open Settings — in the Shop, Hub, Driver, Fleet and Store app, tap your picture, then “Settings”; in the Send app, “Account › Settings”; in the Business app, the menu under your name, then “Settings” — and tap “Unlock with fingerprint or face”.
help.fingerprint-unlock.step2: Type your PIN — in the Shop, Hub and Store app, the account’s password — and tap “Next”. Then tap “Turn it on”, and give the phone your fingerprint or face when it asks.
help.fingerprint-unlock.step3: Next time, the sign-in screen offers “Unlock with fingerprint or face” first. To type the PIN or the password instead, tap “Use my PIN instead” or “Use my password instead”.
help.fingerprint-unlock.step4: To turn it off, open the same row in Settings and tap “Turn it off, use my PIN”, or “Turn it off, use the password”. Nothing else is asked, and you sign in with the PIN or the password as before.
help.fingerprint-unlock.note1: It works on that phone only. Every other phone and browser still asks for the PIN or the password.
help.fingerprint-unlock.note2: Your fingerprint or face never leaves the phone. SeeBuyGet keeps only a key that proves it is that phone.
help.fingerprint-unlock.note3: It is turned off on every phone when the PIN or the password is changed or replaced, and on one phone when that phone is forgotten under “Settings › Phones and browsers”. The sign-in screen then says “Fingerprint or face is off on this phone”: type the PIN or the password, and turn it on again in Settings if you like.
help.fingerprint-unlock.note4: Shop, Hub and Store app: whoever can unlock the phone — with a fingerprint, a face, or the phone’s own PIN or pattern — can then sign in as the shop, the hub or the store without the password. Turn it on only on a phone that is yours alone.
help.fingerprint-unlock.note5: Not on a counter phone: on a shop’s or a hub’s phone where the people at the counter or on the floor sign in, it cannot be turned on, and if it was on, it is turned off the first time one of them signs in there. Settings says why. Each of them signs in as themselves, with their own number and PIN.
help.fingerprint-unlock.note6: No such row in Settings? The phone cannot check a fingerprint or face itself, or your PIN or password does not work on this phone yet. Sign in as before.
help.share-into-chat.title: Send something from another app into a chat
help.share-into-chat.summary: Words or a link from another app — a WhatsApp message with an address, a map link, a tracking link — can go straight into one of your SeeBuyGet chats. On an Android phone, the installed app is in the phone’s share list.
help.share-into-chat.step1: In the other app, tap its share button, and choose the SeeBuyGet app from the list: Shop, Driver, Fleet, Store or Send.
help.share-into-chat.step2: The app opens on “Shared with SeeBuyGet”: what you shared, and your chats, newest first. To change it before it goes, tap “Change the words”.
help.share-into-chat.step3: Tap a chat under “Send it in a chat”. It goes there as a message from you, and like every message it cannot be taken back.
help.share-into-chat.step4: Not for a chat? Tap “Copy”, and paste it wherever you need it.
help.share-into-chat.step5: A photo is never sent loose. Say what it is under “What is this?”, then choose the chat about its load or parcel under “File it to”: it is filed to that load or parcel, marked as from the gallery.
help.share-into-chat.note1: Signed out? What you shared waits on the phone for an hour. Sign in, and choose the chat.
help.share-into-chat.note2: With no signal, it goes by itself when the signal comes back, and the app says it is waiting.
help.share-into-chat.note3: Fleet app: the chats are your drivers’ own, so copy what was shared and pass it on the way you usually do.
help.share-into-chat.note4: The Hub app has no chats, so it is not in the share list.
help.share-into-chat.note5: The app says what you shared did not reach it? Close the app, then share it once more.
help.chat-photos.title: Send a photo in a chat about a load or a parcel
help.chat-photos.summary: A photo in a chat is filed first, then shown. It is kept with the load or the parcel the chat is about — as damage, a paper or proof — with its fingerprint, and the chat shows a card that points to it. A claim about that load or parcel then has it.
help.chat-photos.step1: In the chat, tap “Take a photo” to use the app’s own camera, or “Choose from the gallery” for a photo already on your phone.
help.chat-photos.step2: With the camera, hold the phone still and tap “Take the photo”. Camera blocked? Allow the camera for the app, or choose the photo from the gallery instead.
help.chat-photos.step3: Say what it is under “What is this?”: “Damage”, “A paper” or “Proof”. Proof asks of what: “Loading”, “Handover” or “Delivery” — a parcel is handed over and delivered, never loaded.
help.chat-photos.step4: Tap “File it”. The photo is filed to the load or the parcel with its fingerprint, and the chat shows a card saying where. Once filed, it cannot be taken back.
help.chat-photos.step5: Tap the card to see the photo, who filed it and when, and its fingerprints. “Open in the load’s record”, or the parcel’s, lists every photo filed to it that you can see.
help.chat-photos.note1: Each photo says where it came from: “taken in the app, at the time” for the app’s own camera; “from the gallery, taken … (the phone’s date)” for a photo already on the phone, with the date the phone wrote into it; or “from the gallery, no date on it”. A photo from the gallery is accepted, and only labelled.
help.chat-photos.note2: Who can open it: for a load, its poster and the driver carrying it; for a parcel, the shop, the person collecting it and its sender. SeeBuyGet staff see a load’s photos when a claim is made, or when somebody shares a report of the chat.
help.chat-photos.note3: A claim gathers them. A parcel’s damage claim report carries the photos filed to the parcel, with those filed after it was made handed over beside it. A claim on a load lists the photos filed to the load for the staff who read it.
